atoms.name: Process, program and PCB
atoms.one_line: A process is a program in execution; the PCB stores its state, PC, registers, page-table pointer and open files.

atoms.name: Process states
atoms.one_line: New, ready, running, waiting, terminated; running to ready is preemption, running to waiting is a blocking call, waiting goes only to ready.

atoms.name: Threads versus processes
atoms.one_line: Threads share code, globals, heap and open files; each has its own stack, registers and PC.

atoms.name: Context switch
atoms.one_line: Save the old PCB, load the new one; a process switch changes the address space, a thread switch inside one process does not.

atoms.name: System calls and mode switch
atoms.one_line: A trap moves user mode to kernel mode; system calls, page faults and interrupts cause it, plain function calls do not.

atoms.name: fork() semantics
atoms.one_line: fork() copies the caller; the child gets 0, the parent gets the child pid, and each has its own copy of every variable.

atoms.name: Counting fork() processes
atoms.one_line: n unconditional forks in a row give 2^n processes; with conditions, trace who executes each fork.

atoms.name: Inter-process communication
atoms.one_line: Pipes, message passing and shared memory; shared memory is fastest after setup because no kernel call is needed per access.

atoms.name: wait, exit, zombie and orphan
atoms.one_line: wait() blocks until a child ends; a finished child nobody waits for is a zombie.
